definitions.meaning: to snub or turn someone away curtly
split as RE- plus a word for polish, to shine a second time

explanation.surface: Someone dusts a surface and then shines it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt snub is a brush-off, and buffing something a second time is re-polishing it.

clue.text: Regiment stands — but not its ground

definitions.text: Regiment stands — but not its ground

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regiment of the British Army
to stand someone a drink is to treat them, so stands means treats

explanation.surface: A regiment holds firm, except that it does not hold its position.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a regiment that will not stand its ground falls back. 'Stands' misleads as holding firm; read it as paying for someone's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up ground rather than holding it is a military withdrawal.

parts.note: a beau is an old word for a dandy or fop
a drawn match is a tie, so draws are ties

explanation.surface: A fashionable man attracts attractive young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like a verb meaning attracts, but it is the sporting noun: drawn games are TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely-looking women are called belles, a plural of a word for a lovely person.

indicators.note: destroying the word leaf breaks its letters up so they can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A pest that eats away the leaves of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' wrecks LEAF into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jumping insect that feeds on blood is a classic external parasite.

definitions.meaning: a pearl grown in a farmed oyster is described this way
refined and well educated in taste

explanation.surface: A pearl can come across as refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmed pearls carry this label, and a refined, well-read person is described with the same adjective.

parts.note: under means less than, as in under fifty
takings are the money a shop or business brings in

explanation.surface: Business ventures that bring in smaller returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventures or projects someone takes on are commitments of this kind.

clue.text: The first sign of intelligence in a fool

indicators.note: the first of the word the means only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: wit is quick intelligence, a mark of a clever mind

explanation.surface: The opening hint of brains appearing in an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link: the T simply comes before WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, foolish person is a common British insult of this kind.

definitions.meaning: a fan with spinning blades that turn round
an international service organisation for business people

explanation.surface: Asks for a kind of supporters' association.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric fans with revolving blades are so called, and so is the international service club for professionals.

parts.note: the verb do in its colloquial sense of cheat or swindle someone

explanation.definitionFit: To con or swindle someone is a slang sense of do, and this is an informal word for the same trickery.

definitions.meaning: exchanges one thing for another
skilled occupations such as plumbing or carpentry

explanation.surface: Someone exchanges one occupation for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchanges are deals of barter, and skilled crafts are occupations of the same name.

definitions.meaning: let in or permitted entry
read as in-come, having been let come in

explanation.surface: A question about whether earnings are permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let in or permitted entry fits both, the second read as come in.

clue.text: You may like a nip from this dog

definitions.text: You may like a nip from this dog

parts.words: You may like a nip from this dog
parts.note: a nip is both a bite and a small drink; the Alpine rescue breed is pictured with a cask of brandy at its collar

explanation.definitionFit: The big Alpine rescue breed is famously shown carrying a little barrel of brandy for stranded travellers.

indicators.note: to dish something is to ruin it, so the letters of a set are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a fixed-menu course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like the meal, but as a verb meaning ruin it rearranges A SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking food is consuming it, the everyday verb for having a meal.

definitions.meaning: to wed a woman
an old exclamation of surprise, like indeed

explanation.surface: An archaic speaker vows to wed, indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed someone is the main sense, and an old oath meaning indeed is spelt the same way.

clue.text: Large number leave lesson for exam

indicators.note: the large number departs from the word for lesson, so it is taken out

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of pupils skip a class so they can sit a test.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the M from MORAL; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a language or viva, is named for the mouth.

definitions.meaning: flawless, the best possible
a businessperson might profess ..., two words run together

explanation.surface: Asks what the best job for a business founder might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless as an adjective, and split as I DEAL it is what a trader might profess.

definitions.meaning: the boards are the theatre platform where actors perform
a horse-drawn coach running regular routes

explanation.surface: Someone climbs onto a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre boards are the acting platform, and the old horse-drawn passenger vehicle has the same short name.

parts.note: trips read as light steps of dancing, at a French-named afternoon social occasion with refreshments

explanation.definitionFit: A French term for afternoon tea dances, where trips are the steps danced.

clue.text: He wants to raise the standard of living

definitions.text: He wants to raise the standard of living

parts.words: He wants to raise the standard of living
parts.note: the standard of living here is the ethical quality of conduct, not wealth

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who preaches ethics wants people to live more virtuously.

indicators.note: the bar comes before the time in the answer

parts.note: a lever is a rigid bar used to shift things
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Buying something from a pub before closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' is not buying but grip or mechanical advantage; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or mechanical advantage, the gain a lever gives.

clue.text: Seen in the garden perhaps, incoherent with wine

parts.note: rambling speech wanders without making sense
rosé is a pink wine

explanation.surface: A drunk is spotted in the garden babbling after too much wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous climbing flower is a garden plant one might spot over a fence.

clue.text: An even chance the matador will try to avoid

definitions.meaning: a fifty-fifty situation, as with a coin flip

definitions.text: the matador will try to avoid
definitions.meaning: being thrown into the air by the bull's horns

explanation.surface: A bullfighter tries to dodge a fifty-fifty gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip is an even gamble, and a bullfighter dreads being flung skyward by the horns.

clue.text: A piece played in a mask?

definitions.meaning: a spotted tile used in a game
a small half-mask worn at masquerades

explanation.surface: Someone performs a piece of music in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted game tile and a masquerade half-mask share this name.

parts.note: the player is an instrument, pitch is musical note, and the lead is the note an orchestra tunes to

explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra tunes to the A sounded by this double-reed woodwind.

definitions.meaning: worthless leftovers
sediment, as of coffee, at the bottom of a cup

explanation.surface: Neglected land.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthless residue and the sediment at a cup's bottom both describe the last scraps.

clue.text: New deal for a depressed area

indicators.note: a new version of the word deal has its letters freshly arranged

explanation.surface: A fresh political deal for an economically struggling region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DEAL; 'depressed' means low-lying, not poor; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley is low ground, literally depressed land.

clue.text: Show too much regard for the opposite sex

definitions.text: Show too much regard for the opposite sex

parts.words: Show too much regard for the opposite sex
parts.note: regard read literally as looking, so to look too hard at people one fancies

explanation.definitionFit: To stare lecherously is to look too hard at someone.

indicators.note: the dog chewing up the word kite mangles its letters into another order; the backwards run across the two last words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A stray dog destroys a child's kite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chews up' rearranges KITE; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word for a cur or mixed-breed dog.

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means some different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A fish belonging to a fibrous kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges A STRINGY; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat sea creature with a venomous tail barb is a kind of cartilaginous marine animal.

definitions.note: the definition is a description; the answer is a plural noun for lowest possible values

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A remark that a piece of writing cannot be shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the musical half note, not a jotting; 'article' is the grammar word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest values are the smallest possible, so they cannot be lessened further.

definitions.meaning: continues or advances
the income earned from a sale or event

explanation.surface: Someone continues in order to earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing forward is advancing, and the takings from a sale share this name.

clue.text: Sent her, from the sound of it, to the core of the operation

indicators.note: said out loud, the words sent her are heard as another word

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: Someone was dispatched to the heart of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the sound of it' turns SENT HER into a word said the same way; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The hub of an operation is its middle point or headquarters.
